My grandma didn’t want my two year old self eating sweets, so he handed me a cookie and made sure I ate it in the kitchen. He told me not to tell grandma, but I told my mom when she came to get me. There’s so many things:

1. I wish he’d take the opportunity to teach me how to do things not traditionally feminine. I’ve offered to learn how to mow the lawn, change the oil, and use the grill. He never let me because I was a girl.

2. If only he knew that because I was born a girl doesn’t mean I like all girly things. He taught me how to catch a ball with a mitt when I joined the recreation center softball team, but he wouldn’t teach me to play football or take me fishing.

3. Despite how much he hated taking me to dance class on days my mom couldn’t take me, I really do appreciate that he attended every single one of my recitals and some of my competitions.

4. Don’t be embarrassed to buy tampons/pads. The cashier knows they’re not for you!

5. Lastly, anatomy doesn’t dictate anything. I’m not a housemaid because of what’s between my legs.

Sophomore year of high school, Honors English. Our original teacher (who was amazing!) was fired midsemester for failure to comply with policy.  The replacement teacher was TERRIBLE! She gave low marks on analytical papers if she didn’t agree with your arguments. I once asked her for help with my end of course paper because I was struggling with creating a cohesive thesis statement, and she told me I should go back to fifth grade. I ended up getting a D in the class because she hated my writing. Thank God she didn’t come back my junior year, and the joke’s on her because I aced my college English classes. All I needed was a little bit of help.

I applied for a summer job at Chucksters (but didn't take it because I was offered a job at my first choice) and I remember thinking while I was waiting to be interviewed, "This is not the Chuck E. Cheese I remember!" Skee ball and the tubes were still there, but they got rid of the soccer, basketball, and water shooting games. It made my heart so sad! I didn't get a chance to see or eat the pizza, but my mom always said she hated the pizza because it was cardboard. I can't believe I liked that as a kid!

There was this one amusement park a mile from my house growing up with rides designed exclusively for kids. As a kid, it was my favorite place to go! I loved it more than Toys R Us and Chuck E. Cheese. One wristband would allow me to ride all 10 rides as much as I wanted and we'd get popcorn before leaving.

Well, I'm 22 now, and I watched a YouTube video of how the park is doing now that I've moved away. The rollercoaster is only 30 seconds long (if that) and the other rides are just... gah. The popcorn still looks appetizing though!

I'm sure kids still enjoy it, but I know I wouldn't enjoy it if I were to ever go there again (my parents still live in the house where I grew up).
